title: Engine check screen (device info, NPU/CPU self-test, real-time factor)
description: A diagnostics screen the owner runs on the Q-6690 to confirm the NPU engine works and is fast enough, and to compare it with the CPU engine; the report can be copied and shared (goal 1, PRD acceptance).
steps: Create `enginecheck/EngineCheckRunner.kt`: `data class EngineCheckResult(val engine: String, val initMs: Long, val firstRun: Boolean, val audioMs: Long, val processMs: Long, val text: String, val error: String? = null) { val realTimeFactor: Double get() = if (audioMs == 0L) 0.0 else processMs.toDouble() / audioMs }` and `class EngineCheckRunner(private val factory: TranscriberFactory, private val loadSamples: () -> FloatArray, private val clock: () -> Long)`. `fun run(engine: String): EngineCheckResult`: firstRun = `factory.needsPreparation("en")`; time `factory.create("en")` (initMs); feed `loadSamples()` in 1600-sample chunks to `accept`, then `finish()`, timing it (processMs); text = all Final texts joined by a space; audioMs = samples.size / 16; close the transcriber; any exception → result with `error = e.message ?: e.toString()`.

Create `enginecheck/DeviceInfo.kt`: `data class DeviceInfo(val manufacturer: String, val model: String, val socManufacturer: String, val socModel: String, val hardware: String, val androidVersion: String, val cdspLibraryPresent: Boolean, val htpSkelLibs: List<String>)` with `fun DeviceInfo.Companion.read(context: Context)` (use `Build.SOC_MANUFACTURER`/`Build.SOC_MODEL` on API 31+, else "unknown"; `cdspLibraryPresent` = `File("/vendor/lib64/libcdsprpc.so").exists() || File("/system/vendor/lib64/libcdsprpc.so").exists()`; `htpSkelLibs` = names in `applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir` matching `libQnnHtpV*Skel.so`, sorted) and a pure `fun formatReport(info: DeviceInfo, results: List<EngineCheckResult>): String` producing a plain-text report (one `key: value` per line; per result: engine, first run yes/no, init ms, audio s, processing s, RTF with 2 decimals, verdict, text or error).

Verdict rule (pure function `fun verdict(r: EngineCheckResult): String`): error → "FAILED"; RTF < 0.5 → "OK – fast enough for live transcription"; RTF < 1.0 → "MARGINAL – may lag in long recordings"; else "TOO SLOW for live transcription".

The test audio is the model's own sample: `store.fileFor(ModelCatalog.asrFor("en", engine), "test_wavs/0.wav")` read with `WavReader.readMono16k`. If the engine's English model is not installed, the screen shows "Download the <engine> model first" with a button to `setup` (the setup screen downloads `requiredFor("en", engine)` for the engine being checked — change the setup route to `setup?engine={engine}` with an optional string argument defaulting to null = use the setting, so existing `navigate("setup")` calls keep working, and navigate to `setup?engine=npu` or `setup?engine=cpu` from here).

Create `ui/enginecheck/EngineCheckViewModel.kt` + `EngineCheckScreen.kt` (route `engine-check`): device info card; two buttons "Check NPU" and "Check CPU" (run on `Dispatchers.Default`; while running show "Running… (the first NPU run prepares the model and can take minutes)"); a result card per engine with the verdict prominent; a "Copy report" `TextButton` (clipboard) and a share button (`ACTION_SEND` text/plain with `formatReport`). The checks must not run while a recording is active (`recordingController.state.value.phase != IDLE` → show "Stop the recording first").
Entry point: add a top-bar overflow menu (`Icons.Filled.MoreVert`) to `HomeScreen` with item "Engine check" → `engine-check`.
Write `enginecheck/EngineCheckRunnerTest.kt` (fake factory/transcriber, fake clock advancing by fixed steps) and `enginecheck/ReportTest.kt`.
acceptanceCriteria: Test: with a fake clock where processing 32 000 samples takes 400 ms, the result has audioMs 2000, RTF 0.2 and verdict starting with `OK`
Test: a factory that throws gives `error` set and verdict `FAILED`; the transcriber is closed when accept throws
Test: `verdict` boundaries — RTF 0.49 OK, 0.5 MARGINAL, 1.0 TOO SLOW
Test: `formatReport` contains `socModel: QCS6690` for such a DeviceInfo and `RTF: 0.20`
Route `engine-check` is reachable from the Home overflow menu (visible in `HomeScreen.kt` and `AppNavHost.kt`)
`source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug` exits 0
notes: | Always: run `source scripts/env.sh` before Gradle; the verify command is `source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug`; run `./gradlew --stop` before ending. Never instantiate `com.k2fsa.sherpa.onnx` engine classes (OnlineRecognizer, OnlineStream, OfflineSpeakerDiarization, SpeakerEmbeddingExtractor, ...) in unit tests; plain `*Config` data classes are fine. Only reference sherpa classes inside package `com.convoscribe.engine.sherpa`. Source root: `app/src/main/java/com/convoscribe/`, tests: `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/`.
